transcript.text:
A beeping alarm in a fridge-freezer usually means one of two things: either the appliance thinks a door is open (or not sealing properly), or the temperature inside has risen above a safe level. It’s rarely an electrical fault unless you hear clicking from the back. To narrow this down, please check:
1. Is the freezer door most likely shut tight? Check if anything is blocking it or if the seal looks damaged.
2. Are the contents still frozen solid, or are they softening? If the food is still frozen and the door is shut, try silencing the alarm (usually by holding the 'Alarm' button for 3 seconds, or pressing 'Freeze Temp' depending on your model) and see if it stops. If it starts again after a few minutes, we need to look at why the temperature might be rising.
the bottom drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night, a bag was sticking out. ice cream is a bit soft round the edges but everything else is hard

That explains it perfectly. The alarm was triggered because the drawer wasn't fully closed, letting warm air in and causing that slight softening at the edges of the ice cream. Please push the drawer all the way back in until it clicks or sits flush. Then silence the alarm (usually by holding the 'Alarm' button for 3 seconds, or pressing 'Freeze Temp'). To confirm this was an isolated incident and not a sign of a failing defrost system (which can also cause beeping if ice blocks airflow), please check inside the freezer: is there a thick block of ice on the back wall or coils, or does it look fairly clear with only light frost? If it's clear, just keep an eye on it for 24 hours. If you see heavy ice building up again quickly, let me know and we'll look at the defrost drain.
pressed the button with the bell on it and the beep stopped. not sure about the ice, I can't really tell at the back. the light's still flashing -9 though, going down slowly

Good work silencing the beep. The '-9' you see on the display is likely just showing the current freezer temperature (which can be very cold) rather than an error code, especially since we don't have your model number to confirm what '-9' means specifically for your brand. Since the alarm has stopped and the food is mostly hard, this points back to the door being left open as the main issue. However, because the display was flashing, I want to make sure it wasn't a temporary sensor glitch or that the temperature isn't actually rising. Please keep an eye on it for now:
1. Watch the display: Does '-9' stay steady, or does it continue to flash/change?
2. Check the food again in a few hours: Is everything fully frozen solid once more? If the display stays at -9 and the food refreezes, you're likely fine—just ensure that drawer is pushed all the way in next time. If the temperature reading keeps changing or the food doesn't refreeze, we'll need to look deeper.
ok left it a few hours with the drawer shut. light's stopped flashing now and it says -18

That’s excellent news. It was simply a temporary alarm triggered by the warm air letting in. To stop this happening again, just make sure nothing (like that bag of ice cream) blocks the drawer from sliding fully home. If you have any other questions or if anything else comes up with your appliances, I’m here to help.
